Thanks!

Hi,

I ran one sample and it finished sometime overnight >3hrs.  There is definitely something wrong with what I am doing though.  The methylRaw object only has one row and it says coverage is 922087 (the mean coverage is 78 for this sample).

Thanks in advance!

> myobj<-read( file.list,pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=2,start.col=3,end.col=3,

+              sample.id <http://sample.id>=list("3natural"),assembly="French",
+              treatment=c(0))

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] tileMethylCounts running >1 day
messages.body_plain:
We run a for loop that loops over the chromosomes to get the regions to be summarized, then call the function regionCounts(). You can try GenomicRanges::tileGenome() function with cut.last.tile.in.chrom=TRUE argument and feed the resulting object to regionCounts(). If making tiles is the slow part it this could make it faster.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
you can try to use tileMethylCounts2() function below, it could be faster. Warning, I didn't properly test it. If it fails you might have to debug it and change the code

```
setGeneric("tileMethylCounts2", function(object,win.size=1000,step.size=1000,cov.bases=0)
                   standardGeneric("tileMethylCounts2") )

setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRaw"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){

            g.meth =as(object,"GRanges")
            #chrs   =IRanges::levels(seqnames(g.meth))
            chrs   =as.character(unique(seqnames(g.meth)))
            #widths =seqlengths(g.meth) # this doesn't work with BioC 3.0
            grl=split(g.meth, seqnames(g.meth))
            max.length =max(end( grl  ))
            numTiles=floor(  (max.length-(win.size-step.size) )/step.size )+1

            starts=unlist(sapply(numTiles,function(x) 1+0:(x-1)*step.size ))
            all.wins=GRanges(seqnames=Rle(chrs,numTiles),
                              ranges=IRanges(start=starts,
                                             width=rep(win.size,length(starts))) )

            regionCounts(object,all.wins,cov.bases,strand.aware=FALSE)
          }
)

#' @aliases tileMethylCounts,methylRawList-method
#' @rdname tileMethylCounts-methods
setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRawList"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){

            new.list=lapply(object,tileMethylCounts2,win.size,step.size,cov.bases)
            new("methylRawList", new.list,treatment=object@treatment)

          })

```

messages.subject: calculateDiffMeth glm.fit error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Altuna,

I have run methylKit previously without problems, but now I have one. I run everything as per the tutorial, same format input which is accepted and read in using the mread script on Github, I can make plots for correlation, but then for calling differential methylation I get this error:

> myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
Error in glm.fit(Tmod, X[!is.na <http://is.na>(X)], weights = Y[!is.na <http://is.na>(Y)], family = binomial(link = logit)) :
  object 'fit' not found
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In glm.fit(Tmod, X[!is.na <http://is.na>(X)], weights = Y[!is.na <http://is.na>(Y)], family = binomial(link = logit)) :
  no observations informative at iteration 1
2: glm.fit: algorithm did not converge

Traceback gives:
> traceback()
7: glm.fit(Tmod, X[!is.na <http://is.na>(X)], weights = Y[!is.na <http://is.na>(Y)], family = binomial(link = logit))
6: (function (X, Y, Treat)
   {
       Treat2 = Treat[!is.na <http://is.na>(X)]
       Tmod = model.matrix(~Treat2)
       obj = glm.fit(Tmod, X[!is.na <http://is.na>(X)], weights = Y[!is.na <http://is.na>(Y)],
           family = binomial(link = logit))
       deviance <- obj$null.deviance - obj$deviance
       dispersion = 1
       aliased <- is.na <http://is.na>(coef(obj))
       p <- obj$rank
       if (p > 0) {
           p1 <- 1L:p
           Qr <- obj$qr
           coef.p <- obj$coefficients[Qr$pivot[p1]]
           covmat.unscaled <- chol2inv(Qr$qr[p1, p1, drop = FALSE])
           dimnames(covmat.unscaled) <- list(names(coef.p), names(coef.p))
           covmat <- dispersion * covmat.unscaled
           var.cf <http://var.cf> <- diag(covmat)
           s.err <- sqrt(var.cf <http://var.cf>)
           tvalue <- (coef.p/s.err)[2]
       }
       else if (obj$df.residual <= 0) {
           tvalue = NaN
       }
       wald <- tvalue
       beta1 <- obj$coefficients[2]
       p.value <- 1 - pchisq(deviance, df = 1)
       return(c(wald, beta1, p.value))
   })(dots[[1L]][[8L]], dots[[2L]][[8L]], Treat = c(1, 1))
5: mapply(glm.bare, Ps.list, Ws.list, MoreArgs = list(Treat = Treat))
4: t(mapply(glm.bare, Ps.list, Ws.list, MoreArgs = list(Treat = Treat)))
3: glm.set.v1(subst, set1.Cs, set2.Cs, set1.Ts, set2.Ts)
2: calculateDiffMeth(meth)
1: calculateDiffMeth(meth)

Any ideas?

Thanks, Bruce.
